newsitem.title: USA: U.S. talkshow murder host says surprise not "ambush".
newsitem.headline: U.S. talkshow murder host says surprise not "ambush".

text.p: American talk show host Jenny Jones told a court on Thursday that a programme on same-sex secret admirers after which one guest admitted killing another was not "ambush television."
During more than two hours on the witness stand, Jones also testified that she was not embarrassed about the premise of the show.

Jones was called to testify by lawyers defending Jonathan Schmitz, 26, accused of first-degree murder in the shotgun death of Scott Amedure, 32, on March 9, 1995. The killing happened three days after Amedure revealed his homosexual affection for Schmitz during a taping of the "Jenny Jones" show.
Schmitz, who told the audience watching the show that he was heterosexual, called police to turn himself in, telling them he drove to Amedure's mobile home and shot him twice with a 12-gauge shotgun.
Defence attorney Fred Gibson asked Jones if her show is "ambush television."
Gibson quizzed her on an apology statement the host read on the air several days after the shooting, in which she referred to the show in question as one involving "secret admirers."
Asked by Gibson why she did not reveal the true nature of the show in her apology statement, she said "because the premise of the show was that it was a surprise."

Lawyers for Schmitz are trying to show that he was pushed over the edge and driven to kill his admirer because of mental illnesses and the way he was manipulated on the show. They argue that Jones played a key role in that because of the way she tries to evoke strong reactions from her guests.
If convicted of first-degree murder, Schmitz could be sentenced to life in prison without possibility of parole.
